skill.description: Guides React Native performance reviews across FPS, startup time, bundle size, memory, animations, native modules, and platform profiling.

skill.author: callstackincubator

security_audit.summary: Most static hits are false positives from Markdown examples, React Native documentation, local Gradle or grep commands, and benign PNG screenshots. Two curl-to-bash installer examples are confirmed critical because they execute a remote script, and the remote code loading guide adds a supply-chain concern without integrity controls. No prompt injection text was found in the reviewed files.

remediation.issue: Remote installer is piped directly into bash.
remediation.suggestion: Replace curl-to-bash instructions with a package manager install, a signed release download, or checksum verification before execution.

remediation.issue: Remote code loading examples lack trust controls.
remediation.suggestion: Add guidance for signed chunks, integrity validation, allowlisted hosts, rollback controls, and App Store or Play policy review.

remediation.issue: Local shell commands are presented without execution safeguards.
remediation.suggestion: State that commands should run only with user approval in the project root, and explain what files or build outputs they change.

remediation.issue: Binary screenshots require manual review during marketplace audits.
remediation.suggestion: Keep images as simple documentation assets, strip unnecessary metadata, and avoid embedding instructions or secrets in screenshots.

content.value_statement: React Native performance issues can hide in rendering, startup, bundles, and native code. This skill gives targeted review paths and fixes for common bottlenecks.
actual_capabilities: Maps common symptoms to specific reference guides for JavaScript, native, and bundling work.
Explains profiling workflows for FPS, React renders, native CPU, memory, and startup time.
Provides optimization patterns for FlatList, FlashList, atomic state, Concurrent React, and Reanimated.
Guides bundle analysis, tree shaking, Android R8, Hermes mmap, and app size review.
Documents native module, threading, memory, and platform setup considerations for React Native apps.
limitations: Does not run profilers or inspect screenshots without user-provided tool output.
Does not replace platform-specific benchmarking on real devices.
Some commands require local React Native, Xcode, Android Studio, Gradle, or Expo setup.
Remote code loading guidance requires additional security review before production use.

use_cases.title: Debug scrolling jank
use_cases.description: Find the right FPS, list rendering, and React render checks for a slow screen.

use_cases.title: Reduce release size
use_cases.description: Use bundle, asset, and Android R8 guidance to identify size drivers before release.

use_cases.title: Review native bottlenecks
use_cases.description: Plan profiling for startup time, native modules, memory leaks, and thread usage.

prompt_templates.title: Choose a starting point
prompt_templates.prompt: My React Native app feels slow when users scroll. Use this skill to choose the best references and first checks.

prompt_templates.title: Review render performance
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this screen for avoidable re-renders, list issues, and state patterns. Prioritize fixes with measurable impact.

prompt_templates.title: Analyze startup and bundle size
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me investigate slow startup and a large release bundle. Use this skill to plan measurements and likely optimizations.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a performance remediation
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a phased React Native performance plan for FPS, TTI, memory, bundle size, and native module risks. Include validation steps.

output_examples.input: A feed screen drops frames when users scroll quickly.
output: Start with FPS measurement in a release build.
Check whether ScrollView should be replaced by FlatList or FlashList.
Profile React renders and verify item memoization before changing state architecture.

output_examples.input: An Android app has slow cold startup after adding dependencies.
output: Measure cold starts only and separate JS bundle load from root view render.
Analyze bundle composition and native app size before removing libraries.
Review Hermes mmap, R8, and asset compression settings for Android-specific gains.

output_examples.input: A native module blocks the UI during heavy work.
output: Confirm the blocked thread with native profiling tools.
Move heavy work off the main thread and prefer asynchronous Turbo Module methods.
Re-measure the target interaction after each native change.

best_practices: Measure in release builds on representative devices before and after each change.
Start with the smallest reproducible bottleneck and record the tool output that supports it.
Review security impact before enabling remote chunks, external installers, or new native dependencies.
anti_patterns: Optimizing by adding memoization everywhere without profiler evidence.
Comparing performance while development mode, logging, or simulators distort results.
Copying shell commands or remote installers without verifying source and project impact.

faq.question: Does this skill run performance tools automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance and interpretation patterns. Users must run local profilers or provide their output.

faq.question: Can it help with Expo projects?
faq.answer: Yes. Several references include Expo-specific bundle and tree shaking guidance where it applies.

faq.question: Does it cover native code performance?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes native profiling, threading, Turbo Modules, memory patterns, and Android platform setup.

faq.question: Should I use it before measuring?
faq.answer: Use it to choose measurements first. Apply optimizations after you have baseline results.

faq.question: Does it replace platform documentation?
faq.answer: No. It organizes common React Native performance practices and points to workflows that still need platform tools.

faq.question: Are all commands safe to run?
faq.answer: No. Review each command first, especially remote installers and commands that modify builds or dependencies.
